253041857_bc67bd7e.text: Following data integration, the authors developed a rich, labyrinthine taxonomy of hypothalamic cell populations that first split along the lines of neurons and non-neurons (including oligodendrocyte lineage cells, astrocytes, ependymal cells and microglia). Neurons split into two major clades based on neurotransmitter phenotype (GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons), each of which further split into layers of subclades with increasing granularity, each defined by sets of discriminatory markers that are likely to reflect their developmental history, neurochemistry, connectivity and function. Transcriptionally distinct subpopulations could be linked to both specific anatomical subregions and the dataset of origin using informative data visualizations

253041857_a3ebe269.text: . They focused on two novel, functionally relevant neuronal subpopulations defined by either the G-protein-coupled receptor glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (encoded by Glp1r) or the neuropeptide prepronociceptin (encoded by Pnoc). Their analysis of these specific neuronal subpopulations illustrates the ability of HypoMap to tease out and identify transcriptionally distinct subclasses of neurons within highly heterogeneous populations across anatomical subregions
